title: Majeerteen Sultanate
capsule: The Majeerteen Sultanate was a Somali state in the northeastern Horn of Africa, centred on the Bari and Nugaal regions of what is now Puntland, and ruled by the Osman Mahamuud sub-clan of the Darod Majeerteen. Under Sultan Yusuf Ali Kenadid and his successors in the nineteenth century, the sultanate maintained commercial relations with Oman and Zanzibar and resisted early European encroachment. It signed a protectorate treaty with Italy in April 1889, retaining nominal autonomy while Italy used it as a buffer zone. The Italian colonial campaigns of the 1920s, particularly the 'Campaign of the Sultanates' under Governor De Vecchi, dismantled the sultanate by 1927 and incorporated its territory into Italian Somaliland.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's geographic core is identifiable from Italian colonial and British consular sources, but the precise territorial extent of its tributary relationships in the interior is not cartographically documented.
